transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-06
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Desai (Redwood AE), Elena Park (Redwood SE), Ravi Khatri (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Aurelia CTO), Marco Alvarez (Head of ML), Sophie Ng (Infra), Omar Hassan (Product), Liam Woods (Security)
---
Summary (auto): quick qual on hosting choice for embeddings + rerank, SLOs and security.
---
[00:00] Samir: Great thanks everyone for joining, we'll kick off. I'm Samir with Redwood, Elena and Ravi are here on the SE side. Priya, Marco, good to meet you, thanks for carving out time. Do you want to do a quick intros?
[00:18] Priya: Hey all, Priya here, CTO at Aurelia. We're building a semantic search product for sports analytics, high concurrencies during live games. Marco will cover ML specifics.
[00:32] Marco: Hi, Marco. We're running a hybrid ranker: initial ANN recall from our vector DB then a reranker that uses a 7B model to rescore top 5. Latency budget is tight — user expectation around sub-300 to 400ms end-to-end.
[00:48] Elena: Thanks. Quick note on Redwood offerings: hosted API is fastest to get started, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and reserved GPU pools, Private (VPC / on-prem) for data residency. We'll focus on embeddings + rerank flow and routing.
[01:05] Sophie: For infra context, we have strict egress limits and SSO/SAML. Also we need to ensure KMS integration, we can't allow plaintext keys to leave our perimeter.
[01:22] Samir: Totally makes sense. That's a common ask. We have KMS/HSM integrations and options for customer-managed keys in Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we support BYOK with approved KMS partners — we'll send the exact certs.
[01:35] Marco: Two questions up front: what embedding dims do you recommend? We're currently using 1024 dims from our in-house encoder and experiment with 512 to reduce vector DB storage. Also: when should we quantize?
[01:50] Elena: Good. Dimensionality tradeoffs — 1024 gives better fidelity for subtle similarity but costs on storage and ANN search. 512 often hits a sweet spot for engineering tradeoffs. For high-throughput fanout you can go compact (256) with rerank on a stronger embed or model. Quantization can be effective at query-time for the DB (8-bit PQ) but we caution about quantizing the reranker input if it changes ranking behavior.
[02:15] Marco: Got it. Our flow: embed generation on ingest (batch), store in vector DB (they use a managed milvus today), query-time we do top-100 recall then rerank top-5 with the 7B. We're exploring putting the rerank on hosted Redwood or Dedicated.
[02:33] Ravi: How big is your QPS for queries and for embed ingests?
[02:38] Marco: Peak ingest bursts near 1k/sec during post-game bulk syncs; query QPS avg 120, spikes to 700 during live. Tail latency matters more for queries.
[02:50] Elena: That helps. For the rerank step, tail at 99th percentile drives UX. We typically recommend a Dedicated pool if you need predictable 99p at higher QPS, or hybrid: hosted for general traffic + Dedicated for steady high-throughput rerank lanes.
[03:08] Priya: Can you explain hybrid routing? We saw 'hybrid' in your docs but not sure how it works operationally.
[03:15] Elena: Hybrid top-k routing means requests first go to a low-cost hosted variant; if latency or error rate spikes, traffic is routed to Dedicated or an alternate model automatically. Also you can route critical customers or specific endpoints to Dedicated always. For vector DB integration the idea is you can do recall with your vector DB (milvus) and then call Redwood rerank. If the DB is local to your VPC, we support a VPC peering pattern for Private or Dedicated to minimize hop latency.
[03:44] Sophie: VPC peering would be ideal. Our vector DB is in the same cloud account, we want sub-2ms network hops if possible. What about cold cache and KV cache? We rely on prefix-caching currently at our side.
[03:58] Elena: Redwood has automatic KV cache for model key-value caches which helps decoder speed for chat-like flows; for rerank rescoring you get benefit from batching and model warm pools to avoid cold starts. Cold cache is the main contributor to tail spikes if you have frequent model switches.
[04:18] Marco: For batching, our queries are low-latency interactive, so we don't want to add rebuffering. How does Redwood balance batching with latency SLOs?
[04:27] Ravi: We support latency-aware batching: small window batching and dynamic batch sizing. For example at 120 QPS we can micro-batch at 2-5ms windows without adding 50-100ms. At spikes we scale Dedicated pools or trigger fallback to a faster quantized model for degraded quality.
[04:47] Omar: On quality, how big is the hit from running a quantized rerank model? Marco asked earlier about quantizing embeddings — similar question for the reranker.
[04:55] Elena: Quantization typically trades a few percentile points on rerank accuracy. We recommend doing an eval on your heldout queries. Redwood Optimize can run mini-evals and produce regression alerts. For production, many customers run a slightly quantized model as fallback only while primary is higher precision.
[05:12] Liam: Security question — hosted data residency: can we guarantee logs and telemetry don't contain raw PII? We need audit capability.
[05:20] Samir: We redact inputs in logs by default for hosted, and we provide audit logs and log retention controls for Dedicated and Private. We'll share our security pack that lists what is and isn't stored. Also SSO/SAML for access control and RBAC.
[05:34] Priya: Good. Can you walk through a sample architecture diagram for our flow? Vector DB in our cloud, reranker in Redwood Dedicated or Hosted.
[05:43] Elena: Sure. (Elena shares screen, short pause). Diagram: client -> API gateway -> ANN recall (your Milvus) -> top-k -> Redwood rerank endpoint -> back to client. Option A: Hosted Redwood rerank (fast to stand up) with VPC egress to milvus. Option B: Dedicated with VPC peering to keep traffic internal. Option C: Private: you host the entire control plane and runtime in your VPC/on-prem with customer-managed keys.
[06:22] Marco: Latency numbers — what are typical p99s for a 7B rerank in hosted vs Dedicated?
[06:28] Ravi: On hosted in multi-tenant we see p95 around 45-85ms for 7B and p99 around 220-450ms depending on sequence length and tokenization. Dedicated pools can tighten p99 to under 200ms consistently assuming appropriate shard sizing and warm pools. Those numbers depend heavily on batching, seq length, KV cache misses.
[06:47] Marco: That's in line with what we need. Our rerank input is short — prompt + two docs — so tokens are low.
[06:55] Elena: That helps. Short sequences improve tail significantly. Also consider prefix caching and keeping model instances warm during live hours.
[07:05] Priya: For embed generation at ingest — we need throughput at 1k/sec bursts. Is Hosted ok for that?
[07:12] Samir: Hosted can absorb bursts but sustained high throughput is where Dedicated wins. For periodic high bursts, we can handle burst capacity in Hosted, but the pricing delta and potential throttling windows are factors. Dedicated gives you reserved nodes to handle consistent load and predictable latency.
[07:26] Sophie: Our compliance team prefers Dedicated or Private because of KMS and network controls. How different is the integration effort?
[07:34] Elena: Private takes most integration work — you run more in your environment. Dedicated is a managed offering with VPC peering and less engineering lift. Hosted is minimal lift. We'll help with setup for Dedicated with a runbook and SSO/KMS onboarding steps.
[07:50] Marco: On vector DB connectors — do you push embeddings into vector DB or recommend we keep them proprietarily stored and call Redwood for embeddings on demand?
[07:59] Elena: Common pattern: precompute embeddings for ingestion, store them in the vector DB, and do recall there. At query time you do recall + rerank. On-demand embeddings are for cold items or personalization. If you need consistency across indexing strategies, precompute. If storage is a concern, evaluate dims reduction or product quantization in DB.
[08:20] Marco: Are there out-of-the-box connectors to milvus or pinecone?
[08:25] Ravi: We have reference connectors and a lightweight SDK for common DBs, and we partner with Pinecone in some cases. For managed milvus we provide guidance for sharding and search params to optimize tail. We'll share connector docs.
[08:37] Priya: We want to validate cost for a 6-month pilot with say 50k documents and expected query profile. What's the minimal pilot look like?
[08:45] Samir: Pilot typically: Redwood provisions a Dedicated pool or Hosted trial credits, we run a benchmark with your 50k sample and your queries and measure p50/p95/p99, and we tune batching/quantize profiles. We can give a cost estimate after the first run.
[09:00] Omar: Who from Redwood leads the benchmark?
[09:03] Elena: SE team — that's me and Ravi. We'll run a 2-4 hour benchmark with sample traffic and share results.
[09:10] Priya: SLA question — if we go Dedicated, what uptime and support do you provide?
[09:16] Samir: Dedicated customers get an SLA (we'll attach the specific SLA in the security pack). Typical uptime commitments and incident response windows are included in enterprise agreements.
[09:25] Marco: A detailed question on fallback routing — say Milvus search returns empty or low-quality; can Redwood trigger a different recall strategy or run a broader recall?
[09:34] Elena: You can implement fallback policies: if recall score is low we can expand search radius or switch to an alternate retriever, or call a fallback hosted model. Many customers implement a cascade: local recall -> remote recall -> broader recall. Redwood routing can orchestrate model variants and region fallbacks.
[09:54] Sophie: Networking: we need to confirm egress IP ranges and peering flow. Does Redwood need a set of static egress IPs?
[10:02] Samir: For peering, Dedicated and Private are best. Hosted can use static egress depending on region, we'll provide the IP ranges in the docs. We'll include a checklist.
[10:12] Marco: On evaluation metrics — for rerank we measure MRR and NDCG; will Redwood help run an A/B test during pilot?
[10:19] Elena: Yes, Redwood Optimize supports evals, automatic regression alerts, and A/B rollouts. We can set up experiment hooks to send scored responses and gather metrics.
[10:30] [brief cross talk about calendar scheduling]
[10:44] Priya: One more security: do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO?
[10:48] Samir: Yes we do. We'll include copies of certificates in the security pack.
[10:53] Marco: Small nit: how do you handle model version pinning for rollouts? If we pin a rerank model and then want to roll to a quantized variant as fallback, is that supported?
[11:01] Elena: Yes, model versioning and rollout policies are first-class. You can canary, A/B, or set auto-fallback for error/latency thresholds.
[11:10] Omar: Any gotchas with long term storage of embeddings? We might need to purge older seasons.
[11:15] Elena: Lifecycle policies typically live on the vector DB side; Redwood doesn't store the source embeddings unless you call embedding API and store a copy in Hosted. We'll call out the retention model.
[11:25] Marco: Can we see a sample benchmark report?
[11:28] Samir: We'll send an anonymized benchmark with similar workloads. Elena will attach it.
[11:33] Priya: Ok let's recap and finalize action items.
[11:36] Samir: Recap: Aurelia to share 50k docs + sample query set; Redwood to send security pack, TCO spreadsheet, connectors docs, and propose pilot dates. SEs will run a benchmark and share results. Any blockers?
[11:50] Marco: Timeline: we'd like pilot in two weeks.
[11:54] Elena: We can do that, contingent on us getting data and s3 creds.
[12:00] Sophie: We'll check on egress and peering constraints and get back.
[12:05] Samir: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.
